summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security reviews, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and creating a PR.
summary.outcome: Planning (5 plans, 3 waves, 6 requirements) and execution were completed with all gates green. Simplify, crypto security review, and general appsec review were run, producing several correctness and security fixes. Session ended before CodeRabbit CLI review, remote push, and PR creation.

repo: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — takes raw key bytes, no owner/recipient distinction, reusable verbatim for the shared case.
share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move.
adoptSharedFolderResult must only be called once (for the source result) — calling it for the dest would corrupt the rendered sharedFolderTree view.
SDK collision policy: sdkCore.moveItem throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' (sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:346); no auto-rename needed.
@internal on ensureFolderLoaded is documentation-only; CipherBoxClient is already exported and the method can be called directly from the web.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) must have moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree added — Phase 48 left only 7 methods listed.
File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', NOT FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped, recipient cannot decrypt it).
SDK dist/ is gitignored — CI rebuilds it; no need to commit dist changes.
Web package has no 'typecheck' script — correct command is tsc -b.
useSharedWriteOps.test.ts already existed before phase 49; new handler tests extend it rather than creating a new file.
runWrite swallowed errors and returned void — needed a boolean return to allow callers to conditionally clear selection only on success.
Intel API surface regex extractor is unpopulated — HINT-only artifact, safe to omit from planner prompt when empty.

code.finding: enumerateSharedSubtree DFS did not zero per-iteration folderKey after use, leaving plaintext AES folder keys live in heap across iterations — violates project key-clearing rule. Fixed with try/finally zeroing.
Pick allowlist for SharedFolderClient must have moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree added; Phase 48 only listed 7 methods.
onDownload and onDelete props were required, forcing the shared browser to stub them as no-ops — misleading UX. Made them optional so each button only renders when wired.
Drag-drop self-guard was commented out with a placeholder. Descendant/cycle guard was UI-only (dialog) and not enforced at the SDK layer — a crafted client could still create tree cycles.
runWrite returned void, causing batchMoveItemsHandler to always clear selection regardless of success/failure. Changed runWrite to return boolean so clearSelection is conditional.

workflow: Sequential wave execution without worktrees is the right call for AFK autonomous runs — parallel worktrees introduce merge-base footguns and RAM contention that are hard to hand-drive.
When new public SDK methods are added mid-phase, the SDK dist must be rebuilt before the next wave's web plan runs, or web tsc will fail against stale type declarations.
CodeRabbit CLI review (coderabbit review --agent) should run before PR creation; after the PR is created, CodeRabbit auto-posts a GitHub review addressable via /resolve-pr-reviews.
Automated GSD commits can bypass husky pre-commit hooks — an eslint backstop pass is needed before the PR to catch any lint issues.
The gsd-plan-checker correctly caught a vacuous REQ verify gap (no dedicated web unit test for moveItemHandler) that the planner missed — the iteration loop is worth running.
Scope expansions (batch + drag move) folded in before planner spawn are far cheaper than post-planning scope changes — good timing to catch them during pre-planning.
The /simplify pass correctly deferred behavior-changing findings (cycle guard, clearSelection) to a dedicated correctness commit rather than conflating quality and correctness changes.
security:review (crypto-focused) and security-review (general appsec) cover distinct surfaces and should both be run on crypto-sensitive phases.

friction: 1Password signer wedges on unsigned commits during AFK runs — had to disable local gpg signing (git config commit.gpgsign false) for the session.
gsd-planner revision subagent couldn't commit its own changes because gsd-tools wasn't on its PATH — required a manual commit step after the checker iteration.
Prettier hook reformatted client.ts during the correctness commit, invalidating the planned edit target and requiring a re-read before applying the security zeroing fix.
JSX comment inside a {cond && (...)} expression broke TypeScript compilation — required an extra read-and-fix cycle.
Web package missing a 'typecheck' npm script required discovering the correct tsc -b invocation manually.
Intel API surface extractor was unpopulated, producing an empty artifact that added noise to the workflow without contributing to planning.
The cycle/descendant guard was implemented UI-only in the dialog; general appsec review caught that the SDK layer had no authoritative guard, requiring additional correctness work post-simplify.
